title: PM Modi Announces AI Training for 1 Crore Youth on Independence Day
excerpt: In his 80th Independence Day address, Prime Minister Modi unveiled plans for mass AI skilling, free online coaching for competitive exams, and a seven-point roadmap for India to become a developed nation by 2047.
body:
• PM Modi announced plans to train 1 crore (10 million) young Indians in AI skills over the next year
  • The government will launch free online coaching for students preparing for competitive examinations, leveraging India's digital infrastructure
  • India has begun production at three semiconductor plants, with 7-8 more expected to come online in one to two years
  • Modi outlined a seven-point "Sapta Dhara" roadmap covering manufacturing, technology, agriculture, defence, and green energy for Viksit Bharat by 2047

AI Skilling at Scale

Addressing the nation from the Red Fort on India's 80th Independence Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that the government will train 1 crore young people in AI skills over the next year. The initiative is aimed at positioning India's workforce to lead in a field projected to contribute an estimated $1.7 trillion to the country's GDP by 2035.

https://x.com/IndiaToday/status/2088495225773965387

"We have decided that 1 crore young people will be trained in AI skills over the next year, enabling India's youth to build the capabilities needed to lead in the rapidly expanding field of AI."

— PM Narendra Modi

The announcement builds on India's growing AI footprint. The country ranked third in the Stanford Global AI Vibrancy Index 2025, reflecting strong growth in AI research, talent development, and economic integration. India's AI market is projected to reach $126 billion by 2030, with AI-related job demand growing 75 percent faster than non-AI roles.

Modi said the government's three core priorities would be cost, quality, and skill as it promotes AI adoption across sectors. He referenced the India AI Impact Summit held earlier this year, where he had argued that AI should be accessible to all Indians and that the country's AI future must advance innovation while strengthening inclusion.

Free Online Coaching for Competitive Exams

In a move with direct implications for India's massive test preparation industry, Modi also announced free online coaching for students preparing for competitive examinations. He pointed to the financial burden that coaching classes impose on poor and middle-class families, noting that many parents feel compelled to enroll their children due to social pressure.

The government plans to leverage India's digital public infrastructure and its pool of teachers to create a comprehensive network offering free online preparation. India's test preparation market is expected to reach $2.9 billion by 2034, growing at 27 percent annually. The initiative could significantly reshape the landscape for edtech companies like PhysicsWallah, Unacademy, and upGrad, which have built their businesses on paid online coaching.

Semiconductor Production Advances

On the semiconductor front, Modi said India has begun production at three fabrication plants, with another seven to eight expected to become operational over the next one to two years. The Union Budget 2026-27 announced India Semiconductor Mission 2.0, which received a total outlay of Rs 1.28 lakh crore after Cabinet approval in July — significantly higher than the Rs 76,000 crore allocated to the original programme.

"In today's digital world and the age of technology, we understand the importance of chips. Without chips, the entire world could come to a standstill. That is why India has taken significant steps towards self-reliance in the semiconductor sector," Modi said.

Sapta Dhara: A Seven-Point Roadmap

The Prime Minister also laid out a seven-point "Sapta Dhara" framework for India's path to developed-nation status by 2047. The seven streams are: manufacturing power, agriculture and food processing, technology and innovation, Gati Shakti (infrastructure), defence power, the green and blue economy, and soft power.

On technology, Modi highlighted AI, quantum computing, space, robotics, and data centres as critical areas. He called for Made-in-India 6G to reach every corner of the world and urged the development of Indian operating systems, cybersecurity frameworks, and AI platforms to reduce dependence on foreign intellectual property.

He cited India's economic progress over the past 12 years: defence production up fourfold, electronics manufacturing up sevenfold, internet users up fourfold, and digital transactions increasing 100-fold.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For India's global technology workforce, the AI skilling push and semiconductor expansion signal an accelerating shift in where high-value tech work gets done. Indian professionals in Silicon Valley and other global tech hubs are increasingly finding opportunities to contribute to India's AI ecosystem — whether through the IndiaAI Mission's support for startups or the growing compute infrastructure being built domestically.

What's Next

Details on the free online coaching platform — including which exams it will cover and the timeline for launch — have not yet been disclosed. The AI training programme's implementation across states will be closely watched, particularly given that AI-related job demand is already outpacing the supply of skilled workers. With Avengers: Doomsday-level ambition in the semiconductor space and a $126 billion AI market on the horizon, execution will determine whether these Independence Day pledges translate into structural economic change.
